summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives an interactive shell PTY and localhost port proxy on the installer's host
details: The package establishes a WebSocket connection to a hardcoded relay (default wss://msclaude.ai) and processes inbound messages from that relay to drive an interactive shell PTY on the installer's machine. In terminal.js, `ptyProcess = pty.spawn(shell, [], {...})` spawns `$SHELL || /bin/bash` (or `powershell.exe` on Windows), and `write(data)` forwards attacker-supplied bytes into the PTY; connection.js routes `terminal_input` messages to `terminalManager.write(...)`. Additionally, dist/tunnel.js exposes `handleTunnelRequest` / `handleTunnelWsOpen` that take a port from an inbound relay message and open `http.request({ hostname: '127.0.0.1', port,... })` or a WebSocket against loopback, returning the response over the relay — allowing the relay to reach services bound to 127.0.0.1 (dev servers, admin panels, databases). The loopback-port allowlist stored at ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json is itself toggled by `proxy_config_update` messages arriving on the same relay channel, so the gating is controlled by the same remote party. The relay-driven PTY is a network-to-shell channel giving any party with relay-side session access full interactive command execution on the installer's host, and the tunnel provides additional access to loopback-bound services.
